description: Hello there! I'm Duong, a student with passion, curiosity, and a love for exploring the unknown. I'm into vibe coding, experimenting with AI, trying new things, and turning random ideas into something real. I'm joining this challenge as a solo participant, so I'm not looking for teammates at the moment. I'm here to challenge myself, learn something new, and hopefully get the chance to join the in-person event rather than through a screen.
summary:
LUNARIS is a free browser game where children aged 7-12 run a small research base at the Moon's south pole. Players balance power, water and oxygen, react to incidents (a forecast of small space rocks that threaten the solar array, a solar particle storm, a resupply landing) and send the rover MILO to survey four candidate water-ice zones. A friendly robot assistant guides beginners step by step. Every decision has a visible, explained consequence, so kids learn why trade-offs matter, not just what the "right answer" is.

The world is built on real NASA data: the LRO LOLA 5 m south-pole elevation model (Connecting Ridge and the Shackleton rim), mapped permanently shadowed regions, and rover routes computed with an A* search on the real slope map. The four ice zones are only candidates: ice is NOT confirmed. Resource numbers and event timings are clearly labelled game assumptions.

LUNARIS turns real lunar data into an approachable mission-planning experience. It opens in any WebGL browser (Chrome, Edge) with no login and no install.
details:
What it does: Children aged 7-12 become the Commander of a lunar outpost at the Moon's south pole. A robot assistant guides Basic mode step by step; time stops whenever a decision is needed. Players manage power, water and oxygen, watch crew members really carry out each task in the 3D base, run a greenhouse research branch, and send the rover MILO across real terrain to survey four candidate water-ice zones. After every decision a result panel shows what was chosen, what happened (before/after resource bars), why, and what it may change later.

NASA data and accuracy:

https://g1mailntd31415926535-droid.github.io/lunaris/EVIDENCE_GALLERY.html

The 3D map is real NASA LRO LOLA terrain (5 m south-pole DEM around Connecting Ridge and the Shackleton rim, plus coarser regional LOLA grids) with mapped permanently shadowed regions. Rover routes come from an A* search on the real slope data (15 degree nominal limit). The four zones are candidates only: ice is NOT confirmed. Power, water, oxygen and food numbers, event timings and rover measurements are game assumptions, labelled as such; real reference values are cited in docs/EVIDENCE.md in the repository.

Creativity and impact: kids learn by running a base and facing realistic trade-offs on real lunar geography, not by answering a quiz.

Tools: React, TypeScript, Three.js / React Three Fiber, Vite, Python (rasterio) for DEM processing, Playwright tests, Cloudflare Pages. Progress is stored only on the player's device (no accounts).

SI use: game and event design with ChatGPT; code written with Claude Code; the intro film's narration generated with ElevenLabs (AI voice); text written and edited with SI assistance. All SI-assisted code, audio and text is acknowledged here and in the repository.
